**Ownership:** The atlas search index is owned by the **harbour crew**. Their tech lead is Priya Raman, but she's on sabbatical until October — **Ines Fabre** is standing in for her, so she's the one to loop in for anything requiring a lead's call this week.

**Who to actually talk to:** Day-to-day, stale-index issues go through whoever is on-call — the atlas on-call rotation is weekly, PagerDuty-driven, and hands over Tuesday mornings. I don't have visibility into PagerDuty itself, so I can't tell you the specific name currently on rotation — worth a quick check there rather than assuming it's Ines.

One thing worth flagging before you dig into the "why": my notes have a **direct contradiction** on how the index refresh even works —
- "atlas runs a nightly job at 02:00 UTC to refresh its search index"
- "atlas has no background job queue: everything is request scoped"

Those can't both be true, and it matters for diagnosing an overnight staleness bug (nightly cron failing vs. no such job existing at all). Also relevant: there's a known lesson that **deploys skipping `bin/ship.sh` leave the index stale** and once cost the team an afternoon of downtime — worth checking if last night's deploy went through that script. And separately, the index is rebuilt from Postgres, so worst case it can be safely discarded and regenerated.

Want me to check which of those two job-model claims is actually true by looking at the atlas codebase?
